newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda hopes for higher tea crop through investment.
newsitem.headline: Uganda hopes for higher tea crop through investment.

text.p: Uganda hopes increased investment will boost its relatively small tea harvest to 20 million kg in 1997 from almost 17 million kg in 1996, the Uganda Tea Authority (UTA) said on Wednesday.
Production has risen steadily in recent years, and the UTA said the 1996 harvest compared with less than 13 million kg in 1995.
UTA General Manager Mary Mugabi told Reuters the increase was in large part due to the biggest tea growers, Rwenzori Highlands.
Rwenzori Highlands has a programme to invest $40 million between 1994 and 1998 in a joint venture with the Commonwealth Development Corp, Uganda Development Corp and James Finlay Plc.
In the last 10 years at least $100 million has been invested in tea growing as Uganda sought to diversify away from coffee. But the crop is still less than a tenth that of neighbouring Kenya.
Tea provides only a fraction of Uganda's export earnings, accounting for $17 million in 1996 compared to the $389 million brought in by coffee exports for the 1995/96 season.
Mugabi said the UTA had noted an improvement in quality of Ugandan tea and expressed the hope that it would lead to increased revenues.
"The quality has really improved and although we haven't reached the Kenyan price we think we shall be able to reach that level in one year," she said.
The UTA said Ugandan tea prices averaged $1.16 in 1996 against $1.45 for Kenyan tea.
Mugabi said the biggest problem for Ugandan tea exports is they are bonded in warehouses for auctions at the Kenyan port of Mombasa -- increasing costs and undermining end prices.

East Africa's main port carries virtually all of Uganda's tea exports. A statement from the buyers' group the Uganda Tea Association last month complained Kenya was undermining foreign teas and called for government intervention.

"Apart from taking more time to clear tea from these customs warehouses, extra costs are incurred in the form of bond fees, documentation escorts and agency fees amounting to $0.02 per kilo," the statement said.
